precepts.text: Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness. We spend a lot of time restoring brothers and sisters that fall, bringing them back up, making them better than they used to be. We do it for everybody else.
precepts.point: Is not this thy fear, thy confidence, thy hope, and the uprightness of thy ways? A lot of men walk around saying I am not scared, I will die for this truth. But the real fear goes into unresolved trauma, unresolved issues, things in our past we have not overcome. When we get faced with a challenge, we turn back into that little kid, that boy, that boyfriend that got cheated on, that past marriage.
precepts.why:
Eliphaz says to Job, “Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.” A lot of brothers go out and teach, some at camp 30 days in a row, 100 days, 365 days. We strengthen the weak hands: people come into the body sick and needing help, marriages come in messed up, and we dedicate our time to figuring out how to fix them.

That is Galatians 6:1: “Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.” Brothers will fall, sisters will fall, people in the congregation will fall, and we spend a lot of our time restoring them, bringing them back up, getting them back in position and making them better than they used to be. We do it for everybody else.

As a leader in this truth your phone rings all day: can I counsel with you, I've got a question. We answer, we deal with it, and when we don't know the answer we go to leadership and get counsel for their counsel. “Thy words have upholden him that was falling”: put the cigarettes down, bro; stop smoking weed; see, the Bible says this.

But the verse says, “considering thyself”. Inside our own household we don't do it. Our wife asks a question and we say, go watch 15 minutes with the captains. We deal with everything on the outside, but we are not teaching and building up our own possession. So when it comes upon us, “thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.” You freeze up, you fold up, and you go against your own counsel, because most men don't counsel about what is going on in their own household. The one who restores everybody else has to consider himself too.

precepts.text: There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself. That is what Eliphaz was telling Job: you were the guy that comforted everybody, but now that your turn has come, you are fainting and want to give up. We should all be mindful of that.
precepts.point: But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest: now judgment has come upon you, Job, and now you have given up, you have lost the spirit. Where is that mighty man that helped all the people?
precepts.why:
Eliphaz the Temanite, one of Job's friends, tells him, “Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.” You were the one that strengthened men and women when they were weak; your words upheld those that fell down in grief and in sin. “But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.” Now judgment has come upon you, Job, and now you have given up, you have lost the spirit. Where is that mighty man that helped all the people? Now you're upset, your lips stuck out, you got an attitude.

Sirach says it plainly, and it is something we should all be mindful of: “There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself.” That is what Eliphaz was telling Job. You were the guy that comforted everybody, but now that your turn has come, now that judgment has come upon you, you are fainting and want to give up.

And Job had been that man. He remembered the days “When his candle shined upon my head, and when by his light I walked through darkness”: the commandment is a lamp and the law is light. He was a judge who sat in the gate; young men hid themselves and the aged stood up when he came. “I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him.” He knew what to say to the dying and “caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.” “I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame. I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out.”

That is how Job represents the twelve tribes. What Job went through, we go through as a nation of people, because we were the servants of God, and when the trials came, we gave up, gave in to sin and turned our back on the Lord. The one who taught many has to be profitable to himself when his own trial comes.

precepts.text: Thou hast instructed many and strengthened the weak hands. Build the brothers and sisters up in the spirit.
precepts.point: Think of the faith the Bishop had to have for the truth to be where it is. The impact reaches beyond the purple and gold: outsiders email to donate to the booster club, and every camp watches IUIC at 6 on Saturday night whatever time they teach themselves.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
“Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.” Your job as a leader is to instruct many. And your job is to strengthen the weak hands.

It is your job to build the brothers and the sisters up in the spirit. That is part of how a leader transfers his belief onto others: those who have the rule over you and have spoken unto you the word of God instruct you, and when your hands are weak they strengthen them, so that you can follow their faith.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

points: He couldn't discern the form, or the image, of what he feels. And listen what it says. It stood still, but I could not discern the form thereof. An image was before my eyes. His spiritual eyes. He sees an image. He feels it. Well, look what it says next. Read on. He said, there was silence, but I heard a voice saying something to me. Where was that speech happening? In his spirit. Read on.

That's that inner voice that's speaking. That's that clairaudience, hearing God's voice speaking to him. Now, some of us have experienced that. Now here's the thing. Has any of you experienced that before, where you heard the Lord speaking to you and tell you to not do something, or to do something? Nobody's ever experienced it? Here's the point. If you're spiritual, and you're keeping his commandments sincerely, you better listen to what it's telling you to do. You better listen. That's that spiritual sense trying to guide you and direct your path. And it's not going to direct you to do nothing evil. Again, you have to be spiritual, because if you're not, and you're in the midst of sin doing evil, that could be Satan guiding you and telling you to do wrong. All right, drop that clairaudience. Give me clairsentience.

How many times has a brother come to you and you said, let me go to the scripture right here, the Bible says this, put the cigarettes down, stop smoking weed. As a leader in this truth your phone rings all day: can I counsel with you, I have a question. We even go get counsel for our counsel.

But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled. All the things you have been dedicating your life to help and fix and build up, and now you have something going on in your own household and you do not know what to do. You freeze up; you fold up. You spend months and years building up other people's households with ease, scriptures coming from everywhere, but when it comes on you, you go against your own counsel, because most men do not counsel about issues in their own household.

Is not this thy fear, thy confidence, thy hope, and the uprightness of thy ways? A lot of men walk around saying I am not scared, I will die for this truth. But the real fear goes into unresolved trauma, unresolved issues, things in our past we have not overcome. When we get faced with a challenge, we turn back into that little kid, that boy, that boyfriend that got cheated on, that past marriage.

Eliphaz the Temanite, one of Job's friends, answers him. Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands. You were the one that strengthened men and women when they were weak. Thy words have upholden him that was falling, and thou hast strengthened the feeble knees.
But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest: now judgment has come upon you, Job, and now you have given up, you have lost the spirit. Where is that mighty man that helped all the people?

Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered: if we assay to commune with thee, wilt thou be grieved? But who can withhold himself from speaking? Eliphaz is like, you go to visit somebody that is sick and you do not want to say the wrong thing, but we just cannot sit here and say nothing.

Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands; thy words have upholden him that was falling, and thou hast strengthened the feeble knees. But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.

Is not this thy fear, thy confidence, thy hope, and the uprightness of thy ways? Eliphaz is saying, you used to uplift people, and now trouble is coming upon you and you are about to lose your mind. Maybe you did something. Sometimes it is something we did, but a lot of times it is not; it is for us to go through something because we can handle it, and be a shining example to the next person.
Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished, being innocent? Or where were the righteous cut off? Even as I have seen, they that plow iniquity, and sow wickedness, reap the same.

By the blast of God they perish, and by the breath of his nostrils are they consumed. The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions, are broken. The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, and the stout lion's whelps are scattered abroad.

Now a thing was secretly brought to me, and mine ear received a little thereof. In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falleth on men. Now it is talking about the dreams that we have.

Fear came upon me, and trembling, which made all my bones to shake. Then a spirit passed before my face; the hair of my flesh stood up. It stood still, but I could not discern the form thereof; an image was before mine eyes, there was silence, and I heard a voice.
Saying, shall mortal man be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his maker? Behold, he put no trust in his servants, and his angels he charged with folly.

How much less in them that dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, which are crushed before the moth? They are destroyed from morning to evening; they perish for ever without any regarding it. Doth not their excellency which is in them go away? They die, even without wisdom.
